rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor emigrants phrase is an apposition to the near kin, and ما is coordinated with it; since the Messenger is not called poor, those who include wealthy kin restrict the apposition to what follows.
rows.anchor: بدل من { ذا القربى } و { ما } عطف عليه فإن { الرسول } لا يسمى فقيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fayʾ in this passage is the fayʾ of Banū al-Naḍīr.
rows.anchor: والفيء بفيء بني النضير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan unbelievers expelled the emigrants from their homes and seized their property.
rows.anchor: فإن كفار مكة أخرجوهم وأخذوا أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's bounty and approval is a circumstantial phrase qualifying their expulsion and magnifying their standing.
rows.anchor: حال مقيدة لإخراجهم بما يوجب تفخيم شأنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They support God and His Messenger with their persons and their property.
rows.anchor: وينصرون الله ورسوله } بأنفسهم وأموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their designation as truthful means that they are truthful in their faith.
rows.anchor: أولئك هم الصدقون } في إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is coordinated with the emigrants and refers to the Helpers, whose commitment was manifest in settling in Medina and in faith.
rows.anchor: عطف على المهاجرين، والمراد بهم الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing supplies a deleted noun in the second phrase and a deleted genitive in the first, compensated by the lām; another takes it as settling the abode and sincerely embracing faith, illustrated by an unattributed poetic line.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى تبوءوا دار الهجرة ودار الإيمان فحذف المضاف من الثاني والمضاف إليه من الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says Medina was called faith because it is faith's manifestation and destination.
rows.anchor: وقيل سمى المدينة بالإيمان لأنها مظهره ومصيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means before the emigrants' migration; an alternate syntactic estimate attaches it to settling the abode while faith is a separate object.
rows.anchor: من قبلهم } من قبل هجرة المهاجرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Helpers love those who migrated to them and do not find them burdensome.
rows.anchor: يحبون من هاجر إليهم } ولا يثقل عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here حاجة is whatever need gives rise to, such as a request, resentment, envy, or anger.
rows.anchor: ما تحمل عليه الحاجة كالطلب والحزازة والحسد والغيظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What was given to the emigrants means their share of fayʾ and other gifts.
rows.anchor: مما أعطي المهاجرون من الفيء وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They put the emigrants ahead of themselves, to the extent that a man with two wives would yield one and marry her to an emigrant.
rows.anchor: ويقدمون المهاجرين على أنفسهم حتى إن كان عنده امرأتان نزل عن واحدة وزوجها من أحدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṣāṣa means need, from the gaps in a building.
rows.anchor: حاجة من خصاص البناء وهي فرجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One is protected from the soul's avarice by opposing its strong pull toward wealth and aversion to spending.
rows.anchor: حتى يخالفها فيما يغلب عليها من حب المال وبغض الإنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful attain both immediate praise and reward in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: الفائزون بالثناء العاجل والثواب الآجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Quddūs means utterly free of anything that entails deficiency; a variant reads the name with fatḥa, which is another dialect form.
rows.anchor: البالغ في النزاهة عما يوجب نقصانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Salām is safety from every defect and affliction; the verbal noun is used adjectivally for emphasis.
rows.anchor: ذو السلامة من كل نقص وآفة، مصدر وصف به للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muʾmin means the giver of security; a variant with fatḥa means one who is believed in, with a preposition omitted.
rows.anchor: واهب الأمن، وقرىء بالفتح بمعنى المؤمن به على حذف الجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muhaymin is the watcher and guardian of everything; the form is mifʿayl from security, with its hamza changed to hāʾ.
rows.anchor: الرقيب الحافظ لكل شيء مفيعل من الأمن قلبت همزته هاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Jabbār either compels creation to what He wills or sets their condition right.
rows.anchor: الذي جبر خلقه على ما أراده، أو جبر حالهم بمعنى أصلحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutakabbir is exalted above anything that entails need or deficiency.
rows.anchor: الذي تكبر عن كل ما يوجب حاجة أو نقصانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is declared transcendent of association because no one shares any of these attributes with Him.
rows.anchor: إذ لا يشركه في شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khāliq is the one who measures things according to the demands of His wisdom.
rows.anchor: المقدر للأشياء على مقتضى حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bāriʾ brings things into existence free of disproportion.
rows.anchor: الموجد لها بريئا من التفاوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muṣawwir brings things' forms and qualities into existence as He wills.
rows.anchor: الموجد لصورها وكيفياتها كما أراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's names are beautiful because they indicate meanings of excellence.
rows.anchor: لأنها دالة على محاسن المعاني

words: يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Him because He is transcendent of all deficiencies.
rows.anchor: لتنزهه عن النقائص كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These names encompass all perfections, which return to perfection in power and knowledge.
rows.anchor: الجامع للكمالات بأسرها فإنها راجعة إلى الكمال في القدرة والعلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet promises forgiveness of past and future sins to whoever recites Sūrat al-Ḥashr; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الحشر غفر الله له ما تقدم من ذنبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Jumuʿa is Medinan and has eleven verses.
rows.anchor: مدنية وآيها إحدى وعشرة آية

words: يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth glorifies God.
rows.anchor: يسبح لله ما فى السموات وما في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four divine attributes are also read in the nominative as words of praise.
rows.anchor: وقد قرىء الصفات الأربع بالرفع على المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unlettered are the Arabs, most of whom could neither write nor read.
rows.anchor: أي في العرب لأن أكثرهم لا يكتبون ولا يقرؤون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is one of their own, unlettered like them.
rows.anchor: من جملتهم أميا مثلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His recitation of the signs by one who had never read or studied is a sign of his prophethood.
rows.anchor: من كونه أميا مثلهم لم يعهد منه قراءة ولا تعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He purifies them of corrupt beliefs and deeds.
rows.anchor: من خبائث العقائد والأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book and Wisdom mean the Qurʾān and religious law, or the principles of religion from transmitted and rational learning; this alone would suffice as his miracle.
rows.anchor: القرآن والشريعة، أو معالم الدين من المنقول والمعقول

words: وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their former manifest error was idolatry and the corruption of the Jāhiliyya; this shows their need for a guiding prophet and removes the suspicion that he learned from a teacher.
rows.anchor: من الشرك وخبث الجاهلية، وهو بيان لشدة احتياجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here إن is the lightened form of إنَّ, indicated by the lām.
rows.anchor: و { إن } هي المخففة واللام تدل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reckoning is likened to a ruler displaying troops to inspect their condition.
rows.anchor: تشبيها للمحاسبة بعرض السلطان العسكر لتعرف أحوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although this follows the second blast, the modifier 'that Day' can cover the extended time containing both blasts, the swoon, resurrection, reckoning, and entry into Paradise or the Fire.
rows.anchor: لما كان اليوم اسما لزمان متسع تقع فيه النفختان والصعقة والنشور والحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No secret is hidden from God; the display is to disclose people's condition and make justice manifest, not to inform God.
rows.anchor: سريرة على الله تعالى حتى يكون العرض للاطلاع عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, nothing is hidden from people, as in the verse about secrets being tested.
rows.anchor: أو على الناس كما قال الله تعالى

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the verb with yāʾ, with the separation as the reason given.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بالياء للفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of the person given his book in his right hand elaborates the preceding presentation.
rows.anchor: فأما من أوتى كتبه بيمينه } تفصيل للعرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāʾ is a noun meaning 'take'; it has distinct forms for a man, woman, two people, men, and women.
rows.anchor: هاء اسم لخذ، وفيه لغات أجودها هاء يا رجل وهاء يا امرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of hāʾum is omitted, while kitābīya is the object of iqraʾū because that is the nearer governing verb; if it were governed by hāʾum, iqraʾūhu would be expected.
rows.anchor: ومفعوله محذوف و { كتبيه } مفعول { اقرؤوا } لأنه أقرب العاملين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hāʾ in kitābīya and the parallel words is a pause hāʾ, retained at pause and normally dropped in connected speech.
rows.anchor: والهاء فيه وفي { حسابيه } و { ماليه } و { سلطنيه } للسكت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pausing is recommended because the hāʾ appears in the codex; a reading also retains it in connected speech.
rows.anchor: واستحب الوقف لثباتها في الإمام ولذلك قرىء بإثباتها في الوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon is said to be in the heavens collectively although it is in the lowest heaven, because of the relation among them.
rows.anchor: أي في السموات وهو في السماء الدنيا وإنما نسب إليهن لما بينهن من الملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun is likened to a lamp because it removes the earth's night darkness as a lamp removes darkness around it.
rows.anchor: مثلها به لأنها تزيل ظلمة الليل عن وجه الأرض كما يزيلها السراج عما حوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Growing is a metaphor for originating humans from earth because it better conveys their coming into being and formation from it; the fuller construction is abridged by entailment.
rows.anchor: فاستعير الإنبات للإنشاء لأنه أدل على الحدوث والتكون من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied fuller wording is 'He caused you to grow from earth, then you grew'; the verse compresses this by relying on entailment.
rows.anchor: إنباتا فنبتم نباتا، فاختصره اكتفاء بالدلالة الالتزامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning people to earth means burying them.
rows.anchor: ثم يعيدكم فيها } مقبورين. { ويخرجكم إخراجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing people out means resurrection at the gathering.
rows.anchor: ويخرجكم إخراجا } بالحشر، وأكده بالمصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun intensifies the promise, making return as certain as initial creation.
rows.anchor: وأكده بالمصدر كما أكد به الأول دلالة على أن الإعادة محققة كالابداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is made like a carpet for people to move about upon.
rows.anchor: تتقلبون عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Muzzammil is Meccan and is counted as nineteen or twenty verses.
rows.anchor: مكية، وآيها تسع عشرة أو عشرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muzzammil derives from al-mutazammil, one wrapped in clothes; the tāʾ assimilates into zāy, though another reading pronounces it.
rows.anchor: أصله المتزمل من تزمل بثيابه إذا تلفف بها فأدغم التاء في الزاي وقد قرىء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is also read with an open or a kasra mīm, meaning that someone else wrapped him or that he wrapped himself.
rows.anchor: مفتوحة الميم ومكسورتها أي زمله غيره، أو زمل نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name may disparage his sleeping or fearful state at the first revelation, or commend him; he was wrapped in a cloak.
rows.anchor: سمي به النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام تهجينا لما كان عليه فإنه كان نائما، أو مرتعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed wrapped in a cloak spread over ʿĀʾisha, and the verse was then revealed; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان يصلي متلففا بمرط مفروش على عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name may compare him to someone wrapped up and slow because he was not yet practiced in night prayer.
rows.anchor: أو تشبيها له في تثاقله بالمتزمل لأنه لم يتمرن بعد في قيام الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may derive from carrying a load and mean the one bearing the burdens of prophethood.
rows.anchor: أو من تزمل الزمل إذا تحمل الحمل أي الذي تحمل أعباء النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means either rise for prayer or keep up prayer during the night.
rows.anchor: أي قم إلى الصلاة، أو داوم عليها فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mīm is read with ḍamma or fatḥa, for vowel assimilation or ease.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بضم الميم وفتحها للإتباع أو التخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command exempts a small part of the night.
rows.anchor: إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the exception is from 'the night' and half substitutes for 'a little,' the choice is half, more such as two-thirds, or less such as one-third.
rows.anchor: الاستثناء { من اليل } و { نصفه } بدل من { قليلا } وقلته بالنسبة إلى الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, half substitutes for 'the night'; the pronouns refer to a third, allowing that amount, less such as a quarter, or more such as half.
rows.anchor: أو { نصفه } بدل من { اليل } والاستثناء منه والضمير في { منه } و { عليه } للأقل من النصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse makes the pronouns refer to half, with the choice to perform less than half definitively or choose less or more.
rows.anchor: أو للنصف والتخيير بين أن يقوم أقل منه على البت وأن يختار أحد الأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further parse takes the exception from the general number of night hours and permits half, less, or more.
rows.anchor: أو الاستثناء من إعداد الليل فإنه عام والتخيير بين قيام النصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recite slowly and distinctly, articulating letters so the listener can count them; the wording is likened to well spaced teeth.
rows.anchor: اقرأه على تؤدة وتبيين حروف بحيث يتمكن السامع من عدها من قوله ثغر رتل ورتل

words: إِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ سَبْحًۭا طَوِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day brings prolonged movement among duties, so the Prophet should keep night vigil because intimate communion with God requires free time.
rows.anchor: تقلبا في مهماتك واشتغالا بها فعليك بالتهجد، فإن مناجاة الحق تستدعي فراغا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has sabkhan, meaning a heart scattered by distractions, metaphorically from carding and spreading wool fibers.
rows.anchor: أي تفرق قلب بالشواغل مستعار من سبخ الصوف وهو نقشه ونشر أجزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God continually by night and day; remembrance includes glorification, declaring unity, praise, prayer, Qurʾān recitation, and studying knowledge.
rows.anchor: ودم على ذكره ليلا ونهارا، وذكر الله يتناول كل ما يذكر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Devote yourself to Him in worship and detach yourself from all else.
rows.anchor: وانقطع إليه بالعبادة وجرد نفسك عما سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun tabtīlan replaces the expected tabattulan for its allusive force and to preserve the verse endings.
rows.anchor: ولهذه الرمزة ومراعاة الفواصل وضعه موضع تبتلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabbi al-mashriq may predicate an omitted subject, or be a subject whose predicate is 'there is no god but He.'
rows.anchor: خبر محذوف أو مبتدأ خبره: { لا إله إلا هو }

rows.speaker: ابن عامر والكوفيون غير حفص ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, the Kūfans except Ḥafṣ, and Yaʿqūb read the phrase in the genitive as an apposition to 'your Lord'; another analysis supplies an oath particle.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر والكوفيون غير حفص ويعقوب بالجر على البدل من ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammatical analysis supplies an oath particle before 'Lord of east and west' and takes 'there is no god but He' as its response.
rows.anchor: وقيل بإضمار حرف القسم وجوابه { لا إله إلا هو }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entrust affairs to Him as a consequence of declaring His exclusive divinity.
rows.anchor: مسبب عن التهليل، فإن توحده بالألوهية يقتضي أن توكل إليه الأمور

words: أَدْنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَىِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُۥ وَثُلُثَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adnā is used metaphorically for less, since what is nearer to a thing is less distant from it.
rows.anchor: استعار الأدنى للأقل لأن الأقرب إلى الشيء أقل بعدا منه

rows.speaker: ابن كثير والكوفيون
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and the Kūfans read naṣfahu and thuluthahu in the accusative, coordinated with adnā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير والكوفيون { ونصفه وثلثه } بالنصب عطفا على { أدنى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group of the Prophet's companions also performed the night vigil.
rows.anchor: ويقوم ذلك جماعة من أصحابك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows the exact measures of night and day; placing God's name first signals exclusivity, supported by the statement that people cannot enumerate it.
rows.anchor: لا يعلم مقادير ساعاتهما كما هي إلا الله تعالى، فإن تقديم اسمه مبتدأ مبنيا عليه { يقدر } يشعر بالاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot calculate the time intervals or keep precise count of the hours.
rows.anchor: أي لن تحصوا تقدير الأوقات ولن تستطيعوا ضبط الساعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants concession to leave the prescribed amount of night vigil and lifts the liability for doing so.
rows.anchor: بالترخص في ترك القيام المقدر ورفع التبعة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean perform whatever night prayer is easy, with Qurʾān naming prayer by one of its pillars; another view says the phrase means recite the Qurʾān itself as easily as possible.
rows.anchor: فصلوا ما تيسر عليكم من صلاة الليل، عبر عن الصلاة بالقرآن كما عبر عنها بسائر أركانها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported account says the earlier option made night vigil obligatory, this verse abrogated that obligation when it became difficult, and the five daily prayers later abrogated this ruling.
rows.anchor: قيل كان التهجد واجبا على التخيير المذكور فعسر عليهم القيام به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a new explanation of the ruling, giving a further reason for its concession; the ruling is repeated in light of it.
rows.anchor: استئناف يبين حكمه أخرى مقتضية الترخيص والتخفيف ولذلك كرر الحكم مرتبا عليه

words: وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those traveling to seek God's bounty are traveling for trade and for acquiring knowledge.
rows.anchor: والضرب في الأرض ابتغاء للفضل المسافرة للتجارة وتحصيل العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase refers to people fighting in God's path.
rows.anchor: وآخرون يقاتلون في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to perform the obligatory prayer.
rows.anchor: وأقيموا الصلاة } المفروضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to pay the obligatory alms.
rows.anchor: وآتوا الزكوة } الواجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good loan means other charitable spending, or paying zakāt in the best manner; the promise of return encourages it.
rows.anchor: يريد به الأمر في سائر الانفاقات في سبل الخيرات، أو بأداء الزكاة على أحسن وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is advanced is better and more rewarding than what is deferred to a bequest at death, or than worldly goods.
rows.anchor: من الذي تؤخرونه إلى الوصية عند الموت أو من متاع الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayran is a second object of tajidūhu and either an intensifier or separator, since afʿal min is definite-like and resists the article; a reading has huwa khayrun as a nominal clause.
rows.anchor: و { خيرا } ثاني مفعولي { تجدوه } وهو تأكيد أو فصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seek God's forgiveness in all circumstances because no person is free of shortcomings.
rows.anchor: في مجامع أحوالكم فإن الإنسان لا يخلو من تفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forgiving and merciful.
rows.anchor: إن الله غفور رحيم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says that reciting Sūrat al-Muzzammil removes hardship in this world and the next; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة المزمل رفع الله عنه العسر في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Muddaththir is Meccan and has fifty-five verses.
rows.anchor: مكية، وآيها خمس وخمسون آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muddaththir is al-mutadaththir, the person wearing a cloak.
rows.anchor: أي المتدثر وهو لابس الدثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that at Ḥirāʾ he heard a call, saw an angel above him between heaven and earth, was terrified, returned to Khadīja asking to be covered, and then Gabriel came; this is why some call it the first revealed sūra. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال «كنت بحراء فنوديت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say he covered himself while pondering after being hurt by Quraysh, or that he was sleeping wrapped in a cloak.
rows.anchor: وقيل تأذى من قريش فتغطى بثوبه مفكرا، أو كان نائما مدثرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative figurative reading takes the name as being covered with prophethood and spiritual perfections, or as hidden at Ḥirāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالمدثر المتدثر بالنبوة والكمالات النفسانية، أو المختفي فإنه كان بحراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading doubles the dāl and takes the word to mean one who was charged with and invested in this matter.
rows.anchor: أي الذي دثر هذا الأمر وعصب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means rise from your bed or stand with earnest resolve.
rows.anchor: من مضجعك أو قم قيام عزم وجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning command is general, or its object is elided and supplied by the command to warn the nearest kin.
rows.anchor: مطلق للتعميم أو مقدر بمفعول دل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object may instead be supplied from the statement that the Prophet was sent to all people as bearer of good news and warning.
rows.anchor: وما أرسلنك إلا كافة للناس بشيرا ونذيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Make your Lord specifically the object of magnification, declaring Him exalted in belief and speech.
rows.anchor: وخصص ربك بالتكبير وهو وصفه بالكبرياء عقدا وقولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that when this was revealed, the Prophet said 'God is greatest' and knew it was revelation; the commentator notes that Satan would not command this. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: روي أنه لما نزل كبر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأيقن أنه الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ in this and the following commands can express a condition: whatever occurs, magnify your Lord.
rows.anchor: والفاء فيه وفيما بعده لإفادة معنى الشرط وكأنه قال: وما يكن فكبر ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the fāʾ marks that the first purpose of rising is to declare God above association and likeness; first know the Creator, then declare His transcendence, which the people already acknowledged.
rows.anchor: أو الدلالة على أن المقصود الأول من الأمر بالقيام أن يكبر ربه عن الشرك والتشبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase either explains the man's defiance or gives its cause: he contrived in his mind what to say against the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: تعليل أو بيان للعناد، والمعنى فكر فيما يخيل طعنا في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may sarcastically express amazement at his calculation, or say he reached the utmost possible accusation, like the idiom wishing death on someone for astonishing bravery.
rows.anchor: تعجب من تقديره استهزاء به، أو لأنه أصاب أقصى ما يمكن أن يقال عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra heard the Prophet recite Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda and praised its eloquence, but after Abū Jahl provoked him he called it magic for dividing families; Quraysh rejoiced. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: روي أنه مر بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقرأ { حم } «السجدة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their turning away and fleeing from hearing the reminder is likened to wild asses in alarm.
rows.anchor: شبههم في إعراضهم ونفارهم عن استماع الذكر بحمر نافرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaswara means a lion; the form faʿūla derives from qasr, to overpower.
rows.anchor: أي أسد فعولة من القسر وهو القهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spread-out scrolls are sheets that can be unfolded and read.
rows.anchor: قراطيس تنشر وتقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh said they would not follow the Prophet until each received a book from heaven addressed by God to that individual and commanding him to follow Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: لن نتبعك حتى تأتي كلامنا بكتاب من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first kalla rebukes their demand for signs.
rows.anchor: ردع لهم عن اقتراحهم الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turn away from the reminder because they do not fear the hereafter, not because they were refused scrolls.
rows.anchor: فلذلك أعرضوا عن التذكرة لا لامتناع إيتاء الصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second kalla rebukes their turning away.
rows.anchor: ردع عن إعراضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is a powerful reminder.
rows.anchor: وأي تذكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever wishes may take heed of it.
rows.anchor: فمن شاء أن يذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means either their remembering or their willing.
rows.anchor: ذكرهم أو مشيئتهم كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explicitly says that human action depends on God's will.
rows.anchor: وهو تصريح بأن فعل العبد بمشيئة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads the verb with tāʾ; both forms are also read with a doubled consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع «تذكرون » بالتاء وقرىء بهما مشددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is worthy of being feared for His punishment.
rows.anchor: حقيق بأن يتقى عقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is worthy of forgiving His servants, especially those who fear Him.
rows.anchor: حقيق بأن يغفر لعباده سيما المتقين منهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet promises ten good deeds per person in Mecca who believed in or denied Muhammad to anyone who recites Sūrat al-Muddaththir; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة المدثر أعطاه الله عشر حسنات بعدد من صدق بمحمد عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke addresses either the Messenger for his habit of haste or humanity for being deceived by the immediate life.
rows.anchor: ردع للرسول عن عادة العجلة أو للإنسان عن الاغترار بالعاجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people love the immediate, worldly life.
rows.anchor: بل تحبون العاجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address shifts to the plural to generalize the rebuke and show that human beings are naturally hasty, although singular 'the human' denotes the species.
rows.anchor: تعميم للخطاب إشعارا بأن بني آدم مطبوعون على الاستعجال وإن كان الخطاب للإنسان، والمراد به الجنس

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر والبصريون
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and the Basrans read both verbs with yāʾ, supporting the generic singular interpretation.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة ابن كثير وابن عامر والبصريين بالياء فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces are radiant and joyful.
rows.anchor: وجوه يومئذ ناضرة } بهية متهللة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They truly see God, absorbed in contemplating His beauty; fronting the object conveys this, and this need not occur in every state, so it does not preclude seeing other things.
rows.anchor: تراه مستغرقة في مطالعة جماله بحيث تغفل عما سواه ولذلك قدم المفعول، وليس هذا في كل الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative 'awaiting His favor' is rejected: expectation is not ascribed to a face, the sentence reading departs from the apparent wording, and this sense of waiting does not take ilā.
rows.anchor: وقيل منتظرة إنعامه ورد بأن الانتظار لا يسند إلى الوجه وتفسيره بالجملة خلاف الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet's line about looking toward a king and sea cannot mean waiting: expectation does not result in a gift.
rows.anchor: بمعنى السؤال فإن الانتظار لا يستعقب العطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bāsira means severely frowning; bāsil is stronger but came to be used mainly for a fierce brave man, grim-faced in intensity.
rows.anchor: شديدة العبوس والباسل أبلغ من الباسر لكنه غلب في الشجاع إذا اشتد كلوحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashaddu khalqan means more difficult to create.
rows.anchor: أصعب خلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After asking whether people or the heaven is harder to create, the passage explains the heaven's construction.
rows.anchor: ثم بين كيف خلقها فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samk is either its height above the earth or its thickness, made loftily extended.
rows.anchor: أي جعل مقدار ارتفاعها من الأرض أو ثخنها لذاهب في العلو رفيعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He leveled it, made it even, or completed it with stars, celestial spheres, and other features; the word can mean setting something right.
rows.anchor: فعدلها أو فجعلها مستوية، أو فتممها بما يتم به كمالها من الكواكب والتداوير وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aghṭasha means darkened, from the verb for night becoming dark; night is attributed to the heaven because its motion brings it about.
rows.anchor: أظلمه منقول من غطش الليل إذا أظلم، وإنما أضافه إليها لأنه يحدث بحركتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing out its ḍuḥā means making the sun's light appear, that is, the daytime, as in the verse about the sun and its ḍuḥā.
rows.anchor: وأبرز ضوء شمسها. كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He spread the earth out and prepared it for habitation.
rows.anchor: بسطها ومهدها للسكنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He brought its water out by making springs gush forth.
rows.anchor: بتفجير العيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marʿāhā means grazing or pasture, though originally it denotes the place where animals graze.
rows.anchor: ورعيها وهو في الأصل لموضع الرعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is separated from its conjunction because it is circumstantial with an implicit qad, or because it explains the earth's spreading.
rows.anchor: وتجريد الجملة عن العاطف لأنها حال بإضمار قد أو بيان للدحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He fears either God, harm from the unbelievers if he approaches the Prophet, or the uneven road because he is blind and has no guide.
rows.anchor: الله أو أذية الكفار في إتيانك، أو كبوة الطريق لأنه أعمى لا قائد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is counted among God's blessings because it is generally a way to eternal life and pure pleasures; burial honors a person and protects him from beasts.
rows.anchor: وعد الإماتة والإقبار في النعم لأن الإماتة وصلة في الجملة إلى الحياة الأبدية واللذات الخالصة والأمر بالقبر تكرمة وصيانة عن السباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase indicates that the time of resurrection is not fixed in itself but entrusted to God's will.
rows.anchor: إشعار بأن وقت النشور غير متعين في نفسه، وإنما هو موكول إلى مشيئته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke is directed at humanity for its conduct.
rows.anchor: ردع للإنسان بما هو عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one, from Adam until now, has completely carried out what God commanded; everyone has some shortcoming.
rows.anchor: لم يقض بعد من لدن آدم إلى هذه الغاية ما أمره الله بأمره، إذ لا يخلو أحد من تقصير ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage moves from blessings intrinsic to the person to external blessings.
rows.anchor: إتباع للنعم الذاتية بالنعم الخارجية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement begins an explanation of how food is produced.
rows.anchor: استئناف مبين لكيفية إحداث الطعام

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kūfans read the hamza with fatḥa, making the clause an included-substitute (badal al-ishtimāl) from the mention of food.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون بالفتح على البدل منه بدل الاشتمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sheets are records of deeds, folded at death and spread out at the reckoning.
rows.anchor: يعني صحف الأعمال فإنها تطوى عند الموت وتنشر وقت الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the sheets are distributed among their recipients.
rows.anchor: وقيل { نشرت } فرقت بين أصحابها

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read with a doubled shīn for emphasis, numerous sheets, or intense dispersal.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي بالتشديد للمبالغة في النشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is stripped away, like a hide peeled from a sacrificial animal.
rows.anchor: قلعت وأزيلت كما يكشط الإهاب عن الذبيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has qāf instead of kāf; the interchange of qāf and kāf is common.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { قشطت } واعتقاب القاف والكاف كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire is kindled intensely.
rows.anchor: أوقدت إيقادا شديدا

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وحفص ورويس
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, and Ruways read the verb with a doubled ʿayn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وحفص ورويس بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden is brought near to the believers.
rows.anchor: قربت من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the response to the repeated 'when'; the extended time includes twelve events, six around the world's end and six afterward, through the requital of souls.
rows.anchor: جواب { إذا } وإنما صح والمذكور في سياقها اثنتا عشرة خصلة ست منها في مبادىء قيام الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs is generic in meaning, as in the saying that a date is better than a locust.
rows.anchor: { نفس } في معنى العموم كقولهم تمرة خير من جرادة
